# [mods] Lighting, aux fuse blocks and dual batteries

> **Some safety-critical values on this page are not confirmed** (marked [Unverified] or [Partial]): they come from one source or are only partly supported. Verify against the factory service manual before use; later runs re-check them against new sources.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Identify the Ign relay source for 12v power available when ignition is on or starting. [t17]

[Partial] Identify the switch type by pole, throw, and operation then check voltage ratings. [t157]

Select an SPST switch or use a DPST switch to isolate both live and neutral wires. [t157]

[Partial] Choose a push-to-make switch and select a push-to-break switch. [t157]

[Partial] Install a single pole double throw switch and use its center off position. [t157]

[Partial] Fit and mount DPST and DPDT switches to operate two on-off switches simultaneously. [t157]

[Partial] Select a switch with independent upper and lower illumination pins for dash lighting integration. [t157]

Use a 4-pin switch to wire a dual-illuminated switch. [t157]

[Partial] Source Carling Contura SPST switches and grab extra jumpers to verify wiring logic. [t157]

Plug the CB radio into an auxiliary power box located in the center console. [t158]

Connect the CB radio directly to the battery for hot and cold wires. [t158]

[Partial] Run a power line from the center console to feed an auxiliary box. [t158]

[Partial] Match wires from the new head unit harness to the Metra adapter wires and crimp or solder connections. [t282]

[Partial] Plug RCA cables from the Metra harness into the back of a Rockford Fosgate head unit and leave speaker wires disconnected. [t282]

Extract three steering control pins from the wiring harness at slots 6, 15, and 16. [t282]

Crimp or solder the extracted pins to appropriate connections on the head unit or ASWC adapter. [t282]

[Partial] Connect the Fakra C Male to SMA Male adapter for GPS functionality. [t282]

Connect the Metra 40-NI12 AM/FM antenna adapter. [t282]

[Partial] Connect the USB A Male to USB Mini B Female cable. [t282]

Follow package instructions to set up the Axxess ASWC steering wheel control adapter. [t282]

Connect the Axxess AX-NIS24SWC-6V adapter for Aux In and Rear Camera. [t282]

[Partial] Ensure the factory microphone receives 5V input in addition to signal wires. [t282]

[Partial] Mount the factory microphone on top of the A pillar near the sunshade. [t282]

[Partial] Verify the airbag light remains connected during dash removal to avoid needing a system reset. [t282]

Install an 80A circuit breaker on the positive wire before it passes through the firewall. [t383]

[Partial] Run a 4awg positive and matching 12/2 awg stranded negative ground wire from the battery. [t383]

Install a Maxi/Mega bolt-down style fuse holder near the battery with a Bussmann AMG-175 High Current Fuse. [t383]

Run two large gauge wires through the firewall to a sealed fuse box mounted in the cab. [t383]

[Partial] Tap into the dash light circuit and use a T-tap connector with a factory grommet. [t383]

[Partial] Choose between a spot beam pattern or flood pattern based on preference. [t923]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Identify the switch type needed based on contact sets (pole), conducting positions (throw or way), and operation method.
2. Check voltage ratings, noting that AC values are higher than DC because current falls to zero frequently.

_Procedure reported by [t157]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t157] [Partial]</summary>

1. Select a Single Pole, Single Throw (SPST) switch for simple on-off power control.
2. Use a Double Pole, Single Throw (DPST) switch if isolating both live and neutral wires is required.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t157] [Partial]</summary>

1. Choose a Push-to-Make (SPST Momentary) switch that returns to the normally open position when released.
2. Select a Push-to-Break (SPST Momentary) switch that returns to the normally closed position when released.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t157] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Install a Single Pole, Double Throw (SPDT) switch to control separate devices in two positions.
2. Use the Center Off version of an SPDT for forward-off-reverse motor control.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t157] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Select a switch with independent upper and lower illumination pins for dash lighting integration.
2. [Partial] Ensure the switch has separate ground pins if wiring two lights together, or use one shared pin.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t157] [Partial]</summary>

1. Use a 4-pin switch where the input pin also serves as power for an upper lamp.
2. Wire a dual-illuminated switch with green on top (headlamp circuit) and red on bottom (switch active).

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t157] [Partial]</summary>

1. Source Carling Contura SPST switches from OTRATTW for specific electrical needs.
2. [Partial] Grab extra jumpers to verify wiring logic before finalizing the installation.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t282] [Partial]</summary>

1. Match wires from the new head unit harness to the Metra adapter wires.
2. Crimp or solder connections as necessary.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t282] [Partial]</summary>

1. Plug RCA cables from the Metra harness into the back of a Rockford Fosgate head unit.
2. [Partial] Leave speaker wires disconnected if using this setup.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t282] [Partial]</summary>

1. Use a small sewing pin or paperclip to extract three specific pins from the wiring harness for steering wheel controls.
2. Push the target pin forward from the wire side and hold it.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t383] [Partial]</summary>

1. Install a main breaker on the positive wire before it passes through the firewall.
2. Connect this 80A breaker to trip if draw exceeds capacity, protecting the fuse block from overheating.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t383] [Partial]</summary>

1. Run a 4awg positive wire from the battery to the main fuse block.
2. [Partial] Route a matching negative ground wire alongside it.

</details>

## Specifications

- **Breaker rating for main run protection**: 80A [t383] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Factory mic voltage requirement**: 5V [t282] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)

- **Pin slot locations on harness**: 6, 15, and 16 [t282] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Steering control pins to extract**: 3 [t282] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Wire gauge for accessory runs**: 4awg positive, 12/2 awg negative [t383] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)
- **Wire gauge for main run through firewall**: 4awg [t383] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Use a slot-style opening for the plug to reduce alternator whine noise when taking off. [t158]
- Note that this method may result in slight alternator hum if not squelched. [t158]
- [Partial] This method is described as definitive with no further discussion needed compared to other options. [t158]
- This setup is described as 'fine' until upgraded, but may transmit alternator noise if not squelched. [t158]
- Use a separate relay box with its own fuses for individual lights and accessories. [t383]
- Use stranded wire instead of solid wire to handle vibration. [t383]
- [Partial] Choose a bolt-down style so you only replace the fuse itself if it blows. [t383]
- [Partial] Mount the fuse box under the seat or outboard of the brake pedal if hood space is tight. [t383]
- Use cable glands for waterproofing and strain relief. [t383]
- [Partial] Use a T-tap connector rather than adding an extra fuse for signal wires. [t383]
- Find a factory grommet near the passenger footwell wall to feed multiple 4 gauge wires through. [t383]
